articles.title: Language of Birds
paragraphs: Language of Birds explores the virtues of translation and the desire for communication between humans and birds. Narrated by a storyteller from the future, after the sixth extinction, the film observes attempts to establish a possible exchange.

articles.title: Manières d'être vivant
articles.caption: Manières d'être vivant, Baptiste Morizot, La Terre au carré, 2020
paragraphs: Our modernity has distanced us from the rest of the living world, and we no longer pay attention to other species or ecosystems. Through stories of tracking, philosopher Baptiste Morizot invites us to 'get to know' all 'the inhabitants of the Earth' again.

articles.title: I love finding birds' nests, but what's in them troubles me

image.caption: A Baltimore oriole nest with plastic, Vanya Rohwer

refs.text: Vanya Rohwer, curator, Cornell University Museum of Vertebrates, The New York Times, 2025.

paragraphsAfterGrid: Birds can be choosy about the materials they use to build their nest. Some line their nests with snakeskin to ward off enemies. Others fasten lichens with spider silk to the exterior for camouflage. Still others stuff feathers inside dome-shaped nests of sticks or create false entrances to dupe predators or add aromatic leaves to repel parasites and enhance the immune systems of their nestlings.
Increasingly, and troublingly for what it says about the state of the planet, birds are also using all sorts of plastic litter and other trash to build their nests.<sup class="cit">[1]</sup>

articles.title: Laurent Godet & Vincent Lostanlen
paragraphs: A series of drawings made from bird song spectrograms. Each drawing translates a sound visualisation into a hand-drawn mark — slowing down the reading, making the shape of a call tangible.
